name: Remote Services
summary: Adversaries may leverage remote services to move between assets and network segments. These services are often used to allow operators to interact with systems remotely within the network, some examples are RDP, SMB, SSH, and other similar mechanisms. Remote services could be used to support remote access, data transmission, authentication, name resolution, and other remote functions. Further, remote services may be necessary to allow operators…

analytics.name: Analytic 1936
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies a remote service connection between two Industrial Control System (ICS) network hosts that does not match the documented, approved communication matrix, where the destination host subsequently exhibits process execution or file access inconsistent with normal automated/scheduled inter-host communication. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. analytics.name: Analytic 2159
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies SSH lateral movement between Industrial Control System (ICS) Linux hosts not in the documented communication matrix, with subsequent ICS tool execution or privilege escalation. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.
